Dialogs.Text:
If you mean to reach the forest continent, you will need a ship.
Seek Lesym in Isis. He knows the coast better than anyone here.

Have you found passage across the sea yet?
The forest continent will not wait forever.

You have the look of someone hunting for a ship.
Am I right?

Dialog.Text:
My uncle keeps an old ship in Coast.
Tell him Lesym sent you, and he may let you borrow it.

Dialogs.Text: Safe roads, traveler. Ask at the docks if you need news from Coast.

So Lesym sent you about my ship?
She is old, but she still knows the waves.

Dialog.Text:
I would lend her to you, but someone stole my key.
Find it, and I will open the way to the dock.

Dialogs.Text:
Did you find my key?
Without it, the ship stays locked behind that door.

Dialog.Text:
Bless you. That is the key.
Stand back, and I will open the door to the ship.

Dialogs.Text: The sea is generous to the prepared and cruel to the careless.

I lost my favorite seashell near the shrine.
Please, will you help me find it?

Dialog.Text:
Thank you! I will wait right here.
It has a pale spiral and shines like moonlight.

Oh. I understand.
I will keep looking, but the grass is so tall.

Dialogs.Text:
Did you find my seashell?
I keep thinking I hear it rattling in the weeds.

Dialog.Text:
Please keep looking.
I know it cannot have gone far.

Dialogs.Text:
Thank you for bringing back my seashell.
I will keep it safe this time.
Keep your voice low. Estark the Destroyer stirs beneath these stones. What do you need to know?

Dialog.Text: Estark does not fight like a common beast. He waits for fear to break a party's discipline, then strikes the weakest first. Keep everyone standing.
Old passages, false turns, and guardians that never tire. Search every chamber before you descend, and save your strength for the deepest room.
Readiness is proven below, not spoken here. Go carefully, hero.

Dialogs.Text: Estark must be defeated before darkness spreads beyond the shrine. Have you come seeking counsel?

Dialog.Text: His strength is terrible, but his influence is worse. Creatures grow bolder wherever his shadow reaches, and frightened people begin turning against one another.
Gather allies, sharpen your equipment, and listen closely to those who survived the old battles. Courage without preparation only feeds the darkness.
May the shrine's light follow you into every dark place.

Dialogs.Text: Welcome to the Shrine of Healing. The doors remain open to every wounded traveler.

Dialog.Text: Inside the shrine. Speak plainly about your wounds, and keep enough gold for the road after your treatment.
Safer than the roads, though no sanctuary is beyond Estark's reach forever. Rest while you can.
Walk gently, and leave some peace for the next traveler.

Dialogs.Text: The spring water is cool today. Even a moment beside it can steady the nerves.

Dialog.Text: Not every hurt. It clears the mind and eases weariness, but serious wounds still need the healer's hands.
I help tend the lamps and carry water. Travelers bring enough stories that the shrine never feels far from the world.
May your wounds close quickly and your courage last longer.

Dialogs.Text: The shrine cat watches you with grave suspicion.

Dialog.Text: The cat inspects your fingers, accepts one scratch beneath the chin, then pretends the meeting never happened.
Meow. The cat glances toward the healer, which is either excellent advice or a request for supper.
The cat resumes guarding the warm stones.

Dialogs.Text: Welcome to Coast. Watch the tide, and keep your coin purse close.

Dialog.Text: Most captains will not risk unfamiliar passengers. The old man near the docks owns a vessel, though he guards access to it carefully.
Sailors spend freely, thieves listen closely, and visitors stare at the sea instead of their belongings. An unfortunate combination.
Enjoy the harbor, traveler. Just do it with both eyes open.

Dialogs.Text: Beyond the trees, the desert hides old answers. Bring water, and trust no mirage.

Dialog.Text: Ruins remember what kingdoms choose to forget. Search them carefully and you may learn why Estark's name has returned to frightened lips.
Travel when the heat is kind, mark the direction of the trees behind you, and never follow a distant light merely because it moves.
Good. The desert has buried many confident people.

Dialogs.Text: Welcome to Forest Palace. What brings you beneath our trees?

Dialog.Text: Follow the main path and show respect inside the palace. The court remembers manners almost as long as it remembers favors.
The tower road is dangerous, and scouts saw strange lights above the desert. Keep to marked paths until you know which danger you are chasing.
Then tread lightly. These roots were old before our walls were raised.

Dialogs.Text: Welcome to Isis, crossroads of sand, river, and rumor. What news are you seeking?

Dialog.Text: Even old soldiers lower their voices at that name. If you intend to face him, gather a disciplined party and prepare for a long fight.

Choices.Text: Where can I find a ship?

Dialog.Text: Ask Lesym. He knows the coast and the people who still keep seaworthy vessels.
Then enjoy the city, but remember that rumors often arrive before danger.

Dialogs.Text: Dragons are patient creatures. Never mistake distance for safety.

Dialog.Text: Once, circling beyond the dunes. It watched our caravan for half a day before deciding we were not worth the flame. I have never felt so fortunate to be disappointing.
Spread out, protect your healers, and do not waste your strongest attacks before it commits. A dragon studies you while you panic.
Remembering is easy here. Try it again when the sky has wings.

Dialogs.Text: The sea is dangerous, especially for those who think calm water means a safe journey.

Dialog.Text: Healing supplies, a reliable weapon, and enough patience to wait out trouble. Once you leave shore, every forgotten item becomes important.
Storms, reefs, and creatures large enough to treat a ship as driftwood. The sea does not need monsters to kill you, but it has them anyway.
Good. Venture out only when you are ready to finish the journey.

Dialogs.Text: If a battle turns against you, run. Pride buys more graves than glory.

Dialog.Text: Before your healer falls, before your supplies are gone, and before hope becomes your only plan. Leave enough strength to survive the road back.
Cowards abandon others. Survivors recognize a lost fight and make certain there can be another.
The best advice usually sounds obvious after someone else pays for it.

Dialogs.Text: To defeat Estark, strike quickly and give him no rest.

Dialog.Text: No, but I met someone who escaped. Estark controlled the pace of every exchange until the survivors stopped reacting and forced him to react instead.
Bring companions who can recover under pressure. A single strong warrior becomes a single obvious target.
Preparation is the first blow. Make it count.

Dialogs.Text: Welcome to Oasis. Fill your waterskin before the dunes swallow the road.

Dialog.Text: The busiest road is usually the safest, but storms erase tracks quickly. If the markers vanish, return here instead of guessing.
Creatures hunt near the shade at dusk. They know tired travelers will hurry toward water and forget to look around.
Wise. Thirst turns small mistakes into final ones.

Dialogs.Text: A key waits in the northern tower, though reaching it is no simple errand.

Dialog.Text: A sealed way beneath the city. I do not know what waits beyond it, only that someone worked very hard to keep it closed.
Monsters, old traps, and the impatience that ruins good adventurers. Bring a strong party and search before every step.
Then return with the key, not merely a brave story.

Dialogs.Text: The wall is quiet for now. Do you need directions or a warning?

Dialog.Text: The northern tower lies beyond the upper road. The southern gate opens toward the desert, and neither route forgives careless travelers.
Do not underestimate dragons. Their fire breaks shields first, and their patience breaks formations afterward.
Stone keeps most monsters out, but fear still slips through. People are watching the horizon more than they watch one another.

Dialogs.Text: The man next door has locked himself inside again.

Dialog.Text: He claims something watches his windows after sunset. I told him we live inside a wall, but apparently walls do not impress whatever he imagined.
Knock first. Last time a guard opened the door, he swung a cooking pot at the poor fellow.
Probably kindest. He usually emerges when he runs out of soup.
